title: Automate RBAC bootstrap and tenant role generation for Private installs
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context: Private deployments require repeatable, auditable tenant bootstrapping and least-privilege RBAC bundles. Current manual steps for creating tenant roles, clusterbindings, and initial bootstrap permissions are error-prone during installs and upgrades. This PR automates policy bundle generation and safe application during both fresh installs and in-place upgrades for the Private installer (Helm + Terraform flow).

What this PR does: adds a terraform module to provision cluster-level bootstrap service accounts and a 'rbacctl' helper to generate and validate tenant-specific policy bundles; extends the Helm chart with templated ClusterRole/Role and ClusterRoleBinding/RoleBinding manifests that are gated behind a new chart value (rbac.automateBootstrap). Adds pre-install and post-upgrade Helm hook jobs to run validation and optionally apply bundles via the installer control-plane when running with --auto-apply. Includes a migration path for clusters with legacy role names and a rollback job that removes newly-created bindings if the install fails during the Helm post-install hook.

Key parts: terraform/modules/rbac-bootstrap - idempotent module that creates:
- bootstrap-sa (namespaced + cluster-scoped bindings required for early control-plane tasks)
- optional KMS key IAM grant (for Private entitlements) when kms.enabled = true

helm/redwood-private/templates/rbac-tenant-roles.yaml - parameterized templates for tenant roles with tenancy-scoped verbs; supports a tenancy.selector label to limit scope; supports generating both ClusterRole (for multi-tenant infra privileges) and Role (for tenant-scoped objects).

tools/rbacctl - new small CLI used by CI and the installer to:
- generate policy bundles in YAML from tenant manifest inputs
- run static validations (no wildcard verbs on storage, no cluster-admin grants without explicit approval flag)
- produce migration patches for legacy role name mappings

installer hooks - pre-install job validates the target cluster has required API versions and that the bootstrap SA exists. post-upgrade job applies bundles if --auto-apply is set and triggers a rollback job on failure.

Tests and validation: adds unit tests for rbacctl validations, helm template unit tests (helm-unittest), a new e2e scenario that exercises tenant isolation checks (runs in CI with a short cluster), and terraform integration smoke test for the bootstrap module.

Security / audit notes: all generated bundles include an annotation 'rbac.redwood.com/issued-by: installer' and a fingerprint hash that is checked by the validation step. Default behavior is dry-run; auto-apply requires the new config flag 'rbac.autoApply=true' and an explicit Linear approval (ENG-5891).

Migration & upgrade behavior: older clusters using legacy role names are detected by the pre-upgrade hook which emits migration patches (applied only if 'rbac.applyMigrations=true'). Rollback behavior is implemented as a Helm hook job that removes newly created cluster bindings and restores a marker ConfigMap to the prior state.

Usage notes (how operators run it):
- Fresh installs: helm install with --set rbac.automateBootstrap=true --set rbac.autoApply=false then review generated bundle at /var/lib/redwood/rbac-bundles/<cluster>-<ts>.yaml and apply with 'rbacctl apply' or via the console.
- Auto-apply installs: set rbac.autoApply=true and ensure terraform bootstrap module has created the bootstrap SA and the installer has KMS grant.

Checklist:
- [x] terraform module: idempotent bootstrap resources
- [x] helm templates: parameterized tenant roles + hooks
- [x] rbacctl: generate, validate, and apply paths
- [x] unit + helm template tests
- [x] e2e tenant-isolation smoke test (CI flakiness noted, retried)
- [x] security review items (SEC-214) addressed

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps auto-apply opt-in and preserves a dry-run-first UX to reduce blast radius. Documentation and console integration will follow in a companion PR that consumes the generated bundles for UI approval flow.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Please add a safety check to prevent accidental cluster-admin grants — the validator should fail unless --force-admin is provided and there is an approved Linear ticket.
Aisha Khan: Added the explicit --force-admin check and enforcement of Linear key (ENG-5891) in validator; updated docs to show the approval flow.
Priya Desai: The Helm hook rollback looks good but can you avoid finalizers on the rollback ConfigMap to ensure it doesn't block deletions?
Aisha Khan: Removed finalizer and added an owner-ref pattern for the rollback marker to be cleaned up automatically; added an e2e assertion for marker removal.
Liam O'Connor: Terraform outputs look okay; add a comment about the required provider version (>=3.8.0) so operators don't hit upgrade surprises.
Aisha Khan: Added provider version pin and a short migration note in docs/operator/rbac-bootstrap.md.
release_notes: Automated RBAC bootstrap and tenant role generation for Private installs. Adds terraform bootstrap module, rbacctl generation/validation CLI, Helm hooks for validate/apply/rollback, and e2e tenant-isolation tests. Auto-apply is opt-in. See docs/operator/rbac-bootstrap.md for operator instructions.
additional_notes: Follow-up: UI/console integration to present generated bundles for approval (PM-408) and a companion SDK helper for programmatic applies. Security required a Linear approval for auto-apply of any cluster-admin equivalent bundle (SEC-214).
